problems: Caption: 'The same wheel, smaller, now turns the cart's axle' — there is no cart and no cart axle anywhere in the picture; half the claim is shown by nothing.
Caption: 'so you never saw it turn' — the post is a single still, so nothing shows the wheel turning now either; the claimed improvement (seeing it turn) cannot be seen.
Picture, centre: the upright wooden bearing block stands right in front of the hub, so 'four arms through a hub' is mostly hidden; you see two or three arms and a post covering where they meet.
Picture: the toothed rim meshes with nothing visible — no pinion or second gear engages the cogs, so the teeth read as decoration rather than a gear that drives or is driven.

Picture: the dark drum behind the wheel and the rope coming up from the lower left blur into one muddy brown mass with the wheel; the oak rim, dark arms, drum and table top are all the same brown, so the 'pale hornbeam cogs' are the only part that separates out.

Picture, left: the big workbench with the copper device dominates a third of the frame and pulls the eye away from the wheel; the subject sits on a plain brown octagonal block with no sense of what the winch is or does.
posts.critique: A nice toothed wheel, but the still cannot show the turning it is about, the hub is hidden behind its own bearing post, and the cart the caption promises is simply not in the picture. A gear that touches no other gear looks like a gear-shaped ornament.
